notes: 26M records normalised in 15.8s vs ~6.1 min/pass for the reference (13-23x per frame). Byte-identical to reference on 400k-row samples of all six frames. FOUR BUGS FOUND: (1) the REFERENCE shredded Indic text - normalize_name('प्राइवेट') returned 'पर इव ट' because Python re excludes combining marks from \w while Rust (Polars) includes them; 5.4% train S2 / 6.3% test S2 carry Devanagari. Tokenizer now defined by Unicode category in both engines. (2) unicodedata.combining() returns 0 for Mn marks (e.g. U+0947) and for all Mc, so it was not dropping marks at all; replaced with category L*/M* + single-ASCII-letter fold. (3) Polars replace_all scans non-overlapping, so consecutive duplicate tokens survived - 'Límited Límited' kept one 'limited' and 'S S' kept one 's'; 0.4-0.5% of names diverged. Fixed with \b-anchored alternation. (4) fold table inventoried raw text but folding happens post-lowercase, so French accents went unfolded. Evidence: tests/test_normalize_fast.py.
